evidence.text: The company is building what it calls an “agentic cloud”, infrastructure designed specifically for AI agents rather than adapted for them.

Not promised in policy. Contact us FAQ: Questions, answered 01 What is Granite? Granite is full-stack AI infrastructure, architected from scratch for the agentic era, not adapted from legacy cloud. Two ways in: deploy and own your own dedicated infrastructure with Granite Infrastructure, or consume dedicated compute, storage and an agentic runtime across the network with Granite Web Services. Both run on the same foundation, so the guarantee of control is identical whichever you choose. 02 What does "full control" actually mean here? That your data, your encryption keys and your agentic runtime stay inside the boundary you choose, enforced by the architecture, not promised in a policy document. Nothing leaves that boundary unless you decide it does, and no outside entity can quietly compel access. 03 Can I start on Granite Web Services and deploy Granite Infrastructure later? Yes. It's one foundation, so you can consume capacity on Granite Web Services today and deploy your own unit when the time is right. Deployed Granite Infrastructure units interconnect to become part of the same network. 04 What do I need to host a Granite Infrastructure unit? A prepared pad, a power connection and cooling. The unit is a self-contained, liquid-cooled container that deploys at your chosen site in months rather than years. Final power, GPU and footprint specifications are confirmed against your site. 05 Which AI models can I run? Any of them. Granite Web Services is model-agnostic, bring open-weight or licensed models and swap them as the field moves. Because value sits in the runtime rather than the model, open-weight proliferation works in your favour. And you always keep the keys: not your key, not your agent. 06 Where does my data live, and can I get it out? Wherever you choose, and it stays there by architecture. There's no egress lock-in, so you're never penalised for moving data. 07 What runs underneath both products? A stateless operating layer shared by both products. It makes every node disposable and rebuildable, so control and resilience become properties of the system itself rather than of any single machine. 08 Does Granite help with regulatory compliance? Yes. Granite Web Services ships with a Compliance Pack, controls built into the platform rather than bolted on afterwards, designed to support obligations under major regulatory frameworks. It complements, rather than replaces, your own legal and compliance review. 09 Where are you today, and how do I start? The platform is live and in deployment today, with the first unit shipping in 2026. To begin, talk to us, reserve a node on Granite Web Services, or plan a deployment with Granite Infrastructure.
